title: Observing the Armies on the Battlefield of Kurukshetra
introduction: As the opposing armies stand poised for battle on the sacred field of Kurukshetra, Arjuna, the mighty warrior, sees his intimate relatives, teachers, and friends in both armies ready to fight and sacrifice their lives. Overwhelmed by grief and compassion, Arjuna's strength fails, his mind becomes bewildered, and he gives up his resolve to fight.

title: Contents of the Gita Summarized
introduction: Arjuna surrenders to Lord Krishna as His disciple, and Krishna begins His teachings by explaining the fundamental distinction between the temporary material body and the eternal spiritual soul. The Lord explains the process of transmigration, the nature of selfless service (buddhi-yoga), and the characteristics of a self-realized soul.

title: Karma-yoga
introduction: Everyone must engage in some sort of activity in this material world. But actions can either bind one to this world or free one from it. By acting for the pleasure of the Supreme, without selfish desires, one can be liberated from the law of karma and attain transcendental knowledge of the self and the Supreme.

title: Transcendental Knowledge
introduction: The transcendental knowledge of the soul, of God, and of their relationship is both purifying and liberating. Such knowledge is the fruit of selfless devotional service and is received through disciplic succession. Lord Krishna explains the history of the Gita, the purpose and timing of His descents into this world, and the necessity of approaching an enlightened guru.

title: Karma-yoga — Action in Krishna Consciousness
introduction: Outwardly performing all actions but inwardly renouncing their fruits, the wise person, purified by the fire of transcendental knowledge, attains peace, detachment, forbearance, spiritual vision, and bliss.

title: Dhyana-yoga
introduction: Ashtanga-yoga, a mechanical meditative practice, controls the mind and the senses and focuses concentration on Paramatma (the Supersoul, the form of the Lord situated in the heart). This practice culminates in Samadhi, full consciousness of the Supreme. Krishna declares that the greatest yogi is one who always abides in Him with faith and devotion.

title: Knowledge of the Absolute
introduction: Lord Krishna is the Supreme Truth, the supreme cause and sustaining force of both material and spiritual realms. Advanced souls surrender unto Him in devotion, whereas the bewildered minds turn to mundane pursuits. The Lord reveals His energies and how to perceive Him everywhere.

title: Attaining the Supreme
introduction: By remembering Lord Krishna in devotion throughout one's life, and especially at the time of death, one can attain His supreme abode beyond the material world.

title: The Most Confidential Knowledge
introduction: Lord Krishna is the Supreme Godhead and the supreme object of worship. The soul is eternally related to Him through transcendental devotional service (bhakti). By reviving one's pure devotion, one returns to Krishna in the spiritual realm.

title: The Opulence of the Absolute
introduction: All wondrous phenomena showing power, beauty, grandeur, or sublimity, either in the material world or in the spiritual, are but partial manifestations of Krishna's divine energies and opulence. As the supreme cause of all causes, He is the supreme object of worship for all beings.

title: The Universal Form
introduction: Lord Krishna grants Arjuna divine vision and reveals His spectacular, awe-inspiring Universal Form (Vishwarupa). Thus He establishes His divinity. Krishna explains that His own humanlike two-handed form is the original form of Godhead, unseeable even by the demigods except by pure devotional service.

title: Devotional Service
introduction: Bhakti-yoga, pure devotional service unto Lord Krishna, is the highest and most expedient means to attain pure love for God. Those who follow this supreme path develop divine qualities and become very dear to the Lord.

title: Nature, the Enjoyer, and Consciousness
introduction: One who understands the difference between the body, the soul, and the Supersoul beyond them both attains liberation from this material world.

title: The Three Modes of Material Nature
introduction: All embodied souls are under the control of the three modes, or qualities, of material nature: goodness, passion, and ignorance. Lord Krishna explains what these modes are, how they act upon us, how one transcends them, and the symptoms of one who has attained the transcendental state.

title: The Yoga of the Supreme Person
introduction: The ultimate purpose of Vedic knowledge is to detach oneself from the entanglement of the material world and to understand Lord Krishna as the Supreme Personality of Godhead (Purushottama).

title: The Divine and Demoniac Natures
introduction: Those who possess demoniac qualities and who live whimsically, without following the regulations of scripture, attain lower births and further material bondage. But those who possess divine qualities and conduct themselves by scriptural authority gradually attain spiritual perfection.

title: The Divisions of Faith
introduction: There are three types of faith, corresponding to and evolving from the three modes of material nature. Acts performed by those whose faith is in passion and ignorance yield only impermanent, material results, whereas acts performed in goodness, according to scriptural injunctions, purify the heart and lead to faith in Lord Krishna.

title: Conclusion — The Perfection of Renunciation
introduction: Krishna explains the meaning of renunciation and the effects of the modes of nature on human consciousness and activity. He explains Brahman realization, the glories of the Bhagavad Gita, and the ultimate conclusion of the Gita: the highest path of religion is absolute, unconditional loving surrender unto Lord Krishna, which frees one from all sins, brings one to complete enlightenment, and enables one to return to Krishna's eternal spiritual abode.
